Oh shit that's bad ass I had no idea

That's not a what if. That's actually true. Your brain doesn't directly observe the light, and it doesn't directly hear the noises around you. Nothing comes into direct contact with your brain for it to feel it.

Your eyes have two types of cells, rods and cones. One sees light/dark, and the other type sees color. Light hits these cells, and sets off a chemical reaction that produces electrical signals which travel to your brain, where they are decoded and made sense of. Your ears have tiny hairs in them called cillia that vibrate from pressure changes in the atmosphere. These vibrations work kinda like AC motors in a generator, where they produce electrical signals that are sent to your brain where they are decoded and made sense of. Your skin has nerve cells in them that react to pressure/texture/etc. where they produce electrical signals that are transmitted to your brain where they are decoded and made sense of.

You aren't seeing the world as it is. You are seeing the best guess that your brain can come up with in real time. This is really fun to think about while driving down the interstate at 80 mph.
